title.en: The West, the Mounties and the railway
title.fr: L'Ouest, la Police montée et le chemin de fer

text.en: In the 1920s, some people thought the British islands and territories in the Caribbean Sea should become part of Canada. That did not happen.
text.fr: Dans les années 1920, certains croyaient que les îles et territoires britanniques de la mer des Caraïbes devraient faire partie du Canada. Cela ne s'est pas produit.

source.quote: In the 1920s, some believed that the British West Indies (British territories in the Caribbean Sea) should become part of Canada. This did not occur

verification.evidence: Did you know? In the 1920s, some believed that the British West Indies (British territories in the Caribbean Sea) should become part of Canada. This did not occur, though Canada and Commonwealth Caribbean countries and territories enjoy close ties today.

text.en: Canada's first Prime Minister was born on January 11, 1815, in Scotland. He was still a child when he arrived in Upper Canada.
text.fr: Le premier premier ministre du Canada est né le 11 janvier 1815, en Écosse. Il n'était encore qu'un enfant lorsqu'il est arrivé dans le Haut-Canada.

source.quote: Born in Scotland on January 11, 1815, he came to Upper Canada as a child.

verification.evidence: In 1867, Sir John Alexander Macdonald, a Father of Confederation, became Canada’s first Prime Minister. Born in Scotland on January 11, 1815, he came to Upper Canada as a child.

text.en: Before he led the country, Sir John A. Macdonald worked as a lawyer in Kingston, Ontario. He was a skilled politician and a colourful man.
text.fr: Avant de diriger le pays, sir John A. Macdonald était avocat à Kingston, en Ontario. C'était un politicien habile et un personnage haut en couleur.

source.quote: He was a lawyer in Kingston, Ontario, a gifted politician and a colourful personality.

verification.evidence: In 1867, Sir John Alexander Macdonald, a Father of Confederation, became Canada’s first Prime Minister. Born in Scotland on January 11, 1815, he came to Upper Canada as a child. He was a lawyer in Kingston, Ontario, a gifted politician and a colourful personality.

text.en: Parliament has set aside a day in his honour. January 11 is Sir John A. Macdonald Day.
text.fr: Le Parlement a institué une journée en son honneur. Le 11 janvier est la Journée sir John A. Macdonald.

source.quote: Parliament has recognized January 11 as Sir John A. Macdonald Day.

verification.evidence: Parliament has recognized January 11 as Sir John A. Macdonald Day.

text.en: In Quebec, the main builder of Confederation was Sir George-Étienne Cartier.
text.fr: Au Québec, le principal artisan de la Confédération a été sir George-Étienne Cartier.

source.quote: Sir George-Étienne Cartier was the key architect of Confederation from Quebec.

text.en: In 1869 Canada took over the vast northwest region. Until then the Hudson's Bay Company had held it.
text.fr: En 1869, le Canada a pris possession de l'immense région du Nord-Ouest. Jusque-là, elle appartenait à la Compagnie de la Baie d'Hudson.

source.quote: When Canada took over the vast northwest region from the Hudson’s Bay Company in 1869

verification.evidence: When Canada took over the vast northwest region from the Hudson’s Bay Company in 1869, the 12,000 Métis of the Red River were not consulted.

text.en: The trouble at Red River put Canada's future at risk. If the country could not hold the land in the middle of the continent, it could not stretch from sea to sea.
text.fr: Les troubles de la rivière Rouge ont mis l'avenir du Canada en danger. Si le pays ne pouvait pas tenir les terres du milieu du continent, il ne pourrait pas s'étendre d'un océan à l'autre.

source.quote: future was in jeopardy. How could the Dominion reach from sea to sea if it could not control the interior?

text.en: Ottawa answered the uprising with force. It sent soldiers to take back Fort Garry in 1870.
text.fr: Ottawa a répondu au soulèvement par la force. Le gouvernement a envoyé des soldats reprendre Fort Garry en 1870.

source.quote: Ottawa sent soldiers to retake Fort Garry in 1870.

verification.evidence: In response, Louis Riel led an armed uprising and seized Fort Garry, the territorial capital. Canada’s future was in jeopardy. How could the Dominion reach from sea to sea if it could not control the interior? Ottawa sent soldiers to retake Fort Garry in 1870.

text.en: Louis Riel was elected to Parliament. He never took his seat there.
text.fr: Louis Riel a été élu au Parlement. Il n'a jamais siégé.

source.quote: Riel was elected to Parliament but never took his seat.

verification.evidence: Riel was elected to Parliament but never took his seat.

text.en: Settlers kept moving west, and the rights of the Métis and of First Nations were threatened once more. A second rebellion broke out in 1885.
text.fr: La colonisation poursuivait sa marche vers l'Ouest et les droits des Métis et des Premières Nations étaient de nouveau menacés. Une deuxième rébellion a éclaté en 1885.

source.quote: as Métis and Indian rights were again threatened by westward settlement, a second rebellion in 1885

verification.evidence: Later, as Métis and Indian rights were again threatened by westward settlement, a second rebellion in 1885 in present-day Saskatchewan led to Riel’s trial and execution for high treason

text.en: Riel was put on trial and put to death for high treason. Many people in Quebec were strongly against that decision.
text.fr: Riel a été jugé puis exécuté pour haute trahison. Beaucoup de gens au Québec se sont vivement opposés à cette décision.

source.quote: led to Riel’s trial and execution for high treason, a decision that was strongly opposed in Quebec.

verification.evidence: Later, as Métis and Indian rights were again threatened by westward settlement, a second rebellion in 1885 in present-day Saskatchewan led to Riel’s trial and execution for high treason, a decision that was strongly opposed in Quebec.

text.en: The North West Mounted Police were sent west for two jobs. They were to bring order to the region and to help with talks with First Nations.
text.fr: La Police à cheval du Nord-Ouest a été envoyée dans l'Ouest pour deux raisons. Elle devait y faire régner l'ordre et aider aux négociations avec les Premières Nations.

source.quote: to pacify the West and assist in negotiations with the Indians.

verification.evidence: After the first Métis uprising, Prime Minister Macdonald established the North West Mounted Police (NWMP) in 1873 to pacify the West and assist in negotiations with the Indians.

text.en: The Mounted Police built posts across the West, among them Fort Calgary and Fort MacLeod. Those posts are cities and towns today.
text.fr: La Police montée a établi des postes dans tout l'Ouest, dont Fort Calgary et Fort MacLeod. Ces postes sont aujourd'hui des villes et des villages.

source.quote: The NWMP founded Fort Calgary, Fort MacLeod and other centres that today are cities and towns.

verification.evidence: The NWMP founded Fort Calgary, Fort MacLeod and other centres that today are cities and towns.

text.en: The force needed a base. Regina became the headquarters of the North West Mounted Police.
text.fr: Le corps policier avait besoin d'une base. Regina est devenue le quartier général de la Police à cheval du Nord-Ouest.

source.quote: Regina became its headquarters.

verification.evidence: The NWMP founded Fort Calgary, Fort MacLeod and other centres that today are cities and towns. Regina became its headquarters.

text.en: Some of Canada's best-known heroes served in the Mounties. Major General Sir Sam Steele was one of them.
text.fr: Parmi les héros les plus connus du Canada, certains ont servi dans la Police montée. Le major-général sir Sam Steele était de ceux-là.

source.quote: Some of Canada’s most colourful heroes, such as Major General Sir Sam Steele, came from the ranks of the Mounties.

verification.evidence: Some of Canada’s most colourful heroes, such as Major General Sir Sam Steele, came from the ranks of the Mounties.

text.en: British and American investors paid for the railway across the country. European and Chinese workers built it.
text.fr: Des investisseurs britanniques et américains ont financé le chemin de fer transcontinental. Des ouvriers européens et chinois l'ont construit.

source.quote: The project was financed by British and American investors and built by both European and Chinese labour.

verification.evidence: The project was financed by British and American investors and built by both European and Chinese labour.

text.en: Building the Canadian Pacific Railway took many years of brave, hard work. When its tracks, the "ribbons of steel", were done, a dream shared by the whole country came true.
text.fr: La construction du chemin de fer du Canadien Pacifique a demandé de longues années d'un travail courageux et difficile. Une fois ses voies terminées, ces « rubans d'acier », un rêve partagé par tout le pays s'est réalisé.

source.quote: After many years of heroic work, the CPR’s “ribbons of steel” fulfilled a national dream.

text.en: Canada's economy did well in the 1890s and the early 1900s. It grew larger, and more of the work was done in factories.
text.fr: L'économie du Canada s'est bien portée dans les années 1890 et au début des années 1900. Elle a pris de l'ampleur et s'est industrialisée.

source.quote: Canada’s economy grew and became more industrialized during the economic boom of the 1890s and early 1900s.

verification.evidence: Canada’s economy grew and became more industrialized during the economic boom of the 1890s and early 1900s.

text.en: Newcomers arrived in large numbers during that boom. One million came from Britain and one million from the United States.
text.fr: De nombreux nouveaux arrivants sont venus pendant cette période de prospérité. Un million venaient de Grande-Bretagne et un million, des États-Unis.

source.quote: One million British and one million Americans immigrated to Canada at this time.

verification.evidence: One million British and one million Americans immigrated to Canada at this time.

text.en: The railway made it possible for immigrants to reach the West. Among them were 170,000 Ukrainians.
text.fr: Le chemin de fer a permis aux immigrants de gagner l'Ouest. Parmi eux se trouvaient 170 000 Ukrainiens.

source.quote: The railway made it possible for immigrants, including 170,000 Ukrainians

verification.evidence: The railway made it possible for immigrants, including 170,000 Ukrainians

text.en: Tens of thousands of settlers also came from Germany, France, Norway and Sweden. They settled the West before 1914 and built up farming there.
text.fr: Des dizaines de milliers de colons sont aussi venus d'Allemagne, de France, de Norvège et de Suède. Ils se sont établis dans l'Ouest avant 1914 et y ont développé l'agriculture.

source.quote: tens of thousands from Germany, France, Norway and Sweden to settle in the West before 1914 and develop a thriving agricultural sector.

verification.evidence: Poles and tens of thousands from Germany, France, Norway and Sweden to settle in the West before 1914 and develop a thriving agricultural sector.
